beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which is greater? Fifty or twenty-nine.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Twenty-nine, because nine is bigger than zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each rod is ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each square is one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Line up the tens. Five tens against two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three tens of fifty have no partner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Even nine ones cannot make one more ten.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I looked at the ones first. Fifty has more tens, so fifty is greater.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fifty is greater than twenty-nine. The open side faces the greater number.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which is less? Thirty-one or thirty-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Line up the tens. Three tens and three tens: a tie.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So the first different place is the ones. Line them up.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One is less than two, so thirty-one is less than thirty-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Take away one square, and both numbers are thirty-one.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three tens and one on each side. Thirty-one equals thirty-one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which is greater? Seventy-five or fifty-seven.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Fifty-seven has five tens. I stand at fifty, then step seven.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Seventy-five has seven tens. I stand at seventy, then step five.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Seventy-five is farther right, so seventy-five is greater.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Tens first. Ones only break a tie.
